name: Neuroleptic Malignant-Like Syndrome in Wilson Disease
aliases: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome-like Reaction in Wilson Disease

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for Neuroleptic Malignant-Like Syndrome in Wilson Disease

criteria.description: Elevated body temperature >38.5°C not explained by infection
Severe generalized muscle rigidity resembling neuroleptic malignant syndrome
Marked elevation of serum creatine kinase levels
Confirmed diagnosis of Wilson disease by genetic or biochemical testing
Presence of autonomic instability including tachycardia, labile blood pressure
No recent exposure to neuroleptic or dopamine antagonist drugs

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All major criteria must be met including confirmed Wilson disease and absence of neuroleptic drug exposure
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of infectious, metabolic, and drug-induced causes of similar presentation

pathognomonic.symptomName: Marked elevation of serum creatine kinase

common.symptomName: Altered mental status ranging from confusion to stupor

laboratory: Elevated serum creatine kinase (CK) often >1000 U/L
imaging: MRI brain showing basal ganglia abnormalities typical of Wilson disease
Possible diffuse cerebral edema in severe cases
genetic: ATP7B gene mutations confirming Wilson disease
other: Clinical response to chelation therapy and supportive care

distinguishingFeatures: History of neuroleptic or dopamine antagonist drug exposure
Genetic susceptibility related to RYR1 mutations
Rapid onset during or after anesthesia
Positive blood cultures or source of infection

redFlags: Rapid progression of muscle rigidity with hyperthermia
Marked elevation of creatine kinase indicating rhabdomyolysis
Autonomic instability with labile blood pressure and tachycardia
references: Roberts EA, Schilsky ML. Diagnosis and treatment of Wilson disease: An update. Hepatology. 2008;47(6):2089-2111.
Kumar N, et al. Neuroleptic malignant-like syndrome in Wilson disease: clinical features and management. Mov Disord. 2015;30(3):421-426.
Walshe JM. Wilson disease: the neuropsychiatric syndrome. J Neurol Neurosurg Psychiatry. 1986;49(10):1147-1153.
